dedupe_keys.name: regional shelter analysis for nuclear fallout planning quick start guide

description: This quick-start guide explains how to set up and interpret a Regional Shelter Analysis, which characterises how well the buildings in an area protect occupants from nuclear fallout radiation. It was written by Michael Dillon, D. D. Dennison and P. P. Doshi, published in 2011 and deposited on figshare in July 2017; the deposit warns that the PFscreen model and related data have since been updated while the general method remains relevant. The analysis combines local building databases, knowledge of local building codes and construction, and emergency response planning to rate fallout shelter quality neighbourhood by neighbourhood. Coverage: a general method applicable to any region with building data. Access: one 5.8 MB file on figshare. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: a 2011 guide whose model has been superseded, and the building protection factors themselves are not included. Simulation uses: shelter-in-place versus evacuation planning and estimating radiation exposure of sheltered populations. Related records: the USGS tsunami evacuation dataset and the Kutupalong camp evacuation case study.
